requirements.title: Launcher Destination And Appearance Disclosure
requirements.description: The new-session dialog states which group the session will join on every open, including when opened from a group header's add control, and lets the operator change that destination or create a new group without leaving the dialog. The dialog also names the appearance (colour source, theme, font size) the session will receive before launch.

validation.notes: The destination control renders on every open, reading No group when none is pending

validation.notes: A group header's add control is reflected in the dialog

validation.notes: Create-on-type reaches the caller and selects the new group

requirements.title: Compact Machine Selection
requirements.description: Machine selection in the launcher occupies one trigger row that opens a listbox carrying presence, readiness detail, and grant per row, with a pinned link-a-machine action outside the listbox. Focus returns to the trigger on close.

validation.notes: Trigger, listbox, presence, readiness meta, grant chip, arrow keys, focus return, and the pinned link action outside the listbox
The TargetCard stack is replaced by one trigger row

requirements.title: Group Assignment And Administration Split
requirements.description: Assigning a session to a group and renaming or recolouring a group happen in place through anchored controls. The Manage Groups drawer is an administration surface only: filter, active and empty sections, per-row selection, bulk close, and an empty-group sweep.

validation.notes: Filter, Active and Empty sections, per-row selection, bulk close, sweep, and the absence of any assign control

validation.ref: ui/src/__tests__/tab-bar-rename-group.test.tsx:Add to Group opens the anchored picker, not the manager
validation.notes: Assignment is in place, not a trip through the drawer

validation.ref: ui/src/__tests__/tab-bar-rename-group.test.tsx:moves a grouped pane through the same anchored picker
validation.notes: One picker serves both the add and move cases

requirements.title: Handoff Between Sessions In A Group
requirements.description: One generic verb sends a message from one session to one or more targets in the same group. The composer shows the exact text before sending and reports a per-target sent, queued, or failed result. A handoff is never silently dropped. The send path holds no knowledge of what a payload is and never references the capture-rule matcher.

validation.notes: renderHandoffPrompt substitutes, appends, and never inspects the payload
Per-target results, the queued path, fan-out sequencing, and group-scoped targets
Editable rendered text, multi-select, and queued never reported as sent
A payload sent from one session arrives in another session's terminal output

requirements.title: Waiting Roles
requirements.description: A group holds an ordered list of named roles. A role is running when it holds a session id and waiting when it holds a command and no session id. A waiting role costs no process and no PTY, survives a restart, and renders as a placeholder inside its group block. Roles are optional: every existing grouping behaviour keeps working with no role rows present.

validation.notes: Role lifecycle, ordering, cascade, the partial unique index, and session-recovery reassignment, in both stores
Four role RPCs and their typed error mapping
Roles ride along in one round trip
Store role actions, the running/waiting derivation, and the cascade on group removal
Waiting roles render in their group block, a role-only group stays visible, and running roles are never drawn twice
A two-role template starts one process and leaves one waiting placeholder

requirements.title: Group Auto-Close With Undo
requirements.description: A group closes itself when it holds no panes and no waiting roles. The waiting-role exemption keeps a half-started group alive. Every close, automatic or bulk, is reversible through one undo control for a bounded window, restoring the group, its roles, and its surviving pane assignments.

validation.notes: The waiting-role exemption, undo replay, and the snapshot surviving a failed restore
The closable predicate in isolation

requirements.title: Group Templates
requirements.description: A saved list of role definitions creates a group and its roles in one action. A role's start mode decides whether it starts a process now or waits. Templates are ordinary editable rows with no privileged built-ins; a seeded example is created through the same write path the UI uses and is deletable without breaking any capability.

validation.notes: Role lists at zero, one, and five; validation; use-count preservation; and the seeded example's deletability
Three RPCs, a three-role round trip, and invalid-argument mapping
Group mode seeds from a template, only eager roles start, launcher edits do not touch the stored template, and any template is deletable

requirements.title: Handoff Capture Rules
requirements.description: A named pattern decides when the console offers a handoff. A rule produces a dismissible suggestion and never sends anything. Matching is bounded to a recent window of conversation events. Deleting every rule removes the suggestion surface and leaves every other handoff entry point working.

validation.notes: Rule round-trip, validation, the seeded example's deletability, and seeding skipping a non-empty store
Three RPCs and invalid-argument mapping for all three failures
Glob and regular-expression matching, capture-group payloads, disabled rules, the bounded scan window, and a pathological pattern staying bounded
The chip names its rule, opens rather than sends, and is dismissible
